title: Connexions de Gauss-Manin et équations de Picard-Fuchs. Opération de Cartier : copies de tapuscrit annoté (s.d.), tiré à part (1981), notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: a draft exposition (c. 1970-72) of the crystalline Dieudonné theory of Barsotti-Tate (BT) groups. The previous page stated the deformation theorem (Grothendieck-Messing). For p locally nilpotent on S and a PD-thickening S -> S', BT(S') is equivalent to pairs (G over S, a locally direct summand of D*(G)_{S'} lifting Fil^1 = omega_G).

(1) Reduction to S_o = S (x) F_p. Write S_o = V(p) in S. The ideal pO_S carries canonical divided powers (gamma_n(p) = p^n/n!, which lies in Z_(p)). So S is a PD-thickening of S_o. Applying the theorem to (S_o, S) gives BT(S) = {(G_o over S_o, a lift of the Hodge filtration to D*(G_o)_S)}. This would answer 'Problem 1' (is D* fully faithful, and what is its image over a char-p base?) once one has a description over S_o. Conversely, the general case (S, S') reduces formally to the case (S_o, S). The reason is that the crystalline topos is insensitive to PD-thickenings, so Crisloclib(S) is equivalent to Crisloclib(S_o).

(2) Marginal Problem 3. Find a variant of the deformation theorem for finite locally free p-group schemes. Grothendieck adds: 'I have a candidate'.

(3) Section c), admissible F-V-crystals in char p. Fear: since D*(G_o) carries the Hodge filtration, perhaps Problem 1 should be posed with values in filtered Dieudonné crystals. Claim: in char p the filtration is determined by the crystal with F and V.
- Take phi: (S_o/F_p)_cris -> S_o (Zariski topos). For a char-p PD-thickening (U,T,delta), x^p = p! gamma_p(x) = 0 on the PD ideal. So the absolute Frobenius of T factors through U, and phi^*(E)_T = (T -> U)^* E_U.
- Let M_o be the restriction of M = D*(G_o) to the crystalline site over F_p, and M_{S_o} = epsilon^*(M_o) its Zariski value. Then phi^*(M_{S_o}) = M_o^{(p)}, hence phi^*(Fil^1 M_{S_o}) sits inside M_o^{(p)}.
- From FV = VF = p, the composites in M_o^{(p)} -F-> M_o -V-> M_o^{(p)} -F-> M_o vanish. The stronger claim is that this sequence is exact on every PD-thickening of char p, with Ker V = Im F and Ker F = Im V locally free sub-crystals.
- Continuation on the next page: phi^*(Fil^1) = Ker F = Im V. A fidelity property of phi makes this determine Fil^1 uniquely. 'Admissible' is defined as: such an Fil^1 exists. Crystals of BT groups are admissible, and their Hodge filtration is the canonical one.
- So Problem 1 is reasonably posed with values in unfiltered (admissible) Dieudonné crystals.
errors: The exactness of M_o^{(p)} -> M_o -> M_o^{(p)} -> M_o, with locally free images, is asserted 'pour tout cristal de Dieudonné M'. This is fine over perfect fields: if Vx is in pM = VFM then x is in FM, by injectivity of V. Over reduced bases, ranks are locally constant because rk(F mod p) + rk(V mod p) = rk M pointwise. For an arbitrary F-V-crystal over a non-reduced base, local freeness of Im F / Ker V is not automatic. The published proofs (Berthelot-Breen-Messing, Mazur-Messing) establish it for D*(G) of a BT group. The claim as stated is therefore at best an unproved generalisation; for general crystals it may require a hypothesis.

Using the PD structure on pO_S to apply a deformation theorem requiring nilpotent divided powers is delicate for p = 2 (gamma_2(2) = 2 is not nilpotent in the PD sense). The text glosses over this, consistent with the hedge added on the previous page ('si S' est à p. div. nil...').

ideas.what: Grothendieck-Messing deformation theorem for BT groups via lifts of the Hodge filtration to the Dieudonné crystal
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (Nice ICM 1970, Montréal 1970); proof by Messing (LNM 264, 1972)
ideas.where_published: Grothendieck, 'Groupes de Barsotti-Tate et cristaux', Actes ICM Nice 1970; 'Groupes de Barsotti-Tate et cristaux de Dieudonné', Presses Univ. Montréal 1974

ideas.what: Reduction of the general (S,S') case to (S_o = S mod p, S) using the PD structure on (p) and the invariance of the crystalline topos under PD thickenings
ideas.modern_name: Crystalline invariance under PD-thickening; lifting from S mod p

ideas.what: Problem 3: deformation theory of finite locally free p-group schemes by (filtered) Dieudonné crystals; Grothendieck claims a candidate
ideas.modern_name: Crystalline/Breuil-Kisin/window classification and deformation of finite flat group schemes
ideas.usually_credited_to: de Jong (1993), Breuil (1998-2000), Zink, Kisin, Lau (2000s)

ideas.what: Morphism phi: (S_o/F_p)_cris -> S_o from the factorisation of Frobenius of a char-p PD thickening through its base, with phi^* epsilon^* M = M^{(p)}
ideas.modern_name: Frobenius factorisation through PD-thickenings (as in Berthelot-Ogus, BBM)

ideas.what: Exactness of F/V sequence, and determination of the Hodge filtration by phi^*(omega_G) = Ker F = Im V
ideas.modern_name: Hodge filtration equals image of V / kernel of F in char p
ideas.where_published: Possibly sketched in the Nice 1970 report

ideas.what: Notion of 'admissible' F-V-crystal (or Dieudonné crystal): exists a locally direct summand Fil^1 with phi^*Fil^1 = Ker F; such Fil^1 is unique
ideas.modern_name: Condition singling out the candidate essential image of D* in char p (cf. de Jong's work on full faithfulness and essential image)

missed.claim: Grothendieck states he has a candidate for a deformation theorem for finite locally free p-group schemes. The later theory (Breuil, Kisin, Zink-Lau windows/frames) achieved classification only under restrictions (p>2, regular bases, etc.). Grothendieck's own candidate is not recorded on this page.
missed.quote: Problème 3 Trouver variante du th. de déformation pour les p-Groupes finis loc. libres (j'ai un candidat).
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Deformation theory of finite flat group schemes via crystals remains incomplete in general. If his candidate is described elsewhere in cote 93, it would be historically interesting. It could be compared with Breuil-Kisin modules and Lau's frames.

missed.claim: The intrinsic characterisation of the Hodge filtration via the Frobenius-factorisation morphism phi, and the term 'admissible F-V-crystal', appear here as a programmatic definition. This predates the BBM formulation, and the terminology is not standard in the later literature.
missed.quote: la filtration est uniquement déterminée en termes de la structure de cristal de Dieudonné
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Mainly historical: it documents that Grothendieck had the 'Hodge filtration = Ker F' description and an essential-image condition for Problem 1 early on.

deep.surprise_reason: Mostly the known Grothendieck-Messing / BBM programme in Grothendieck's own early formulation. The notable bits are the explicit admissibility definition via phi and the marginal claim of a candidate deformation theory for finite flat p-groups, which is not in the published record as far as I know.
transcription_corrections: Margin note reads 'Problème 3 Trouver variante du th. de déformation pour les p-Groupes / finis loc. libres (j'ai un candidat)'. The second half is in the left margin, bracketed against the paragraph.
In the diagram the first term is typed M_o^{(p)} with an overstruck letter; the arrows are labelled by hand F_{M_o}, V_{M_o}, F_{M_o}.
The morphism is typed 'phi : S_o cris/F_p -> S_o' with 'cris' overstruck and epsilon handwritten above a curved arrow, indicating phi is related to epsilon.
The struck-out text before 'notons que' is 'le sous-Module Fil'; before 'général' a struck word is 'envisagé'.
